name: While Loops
description: Repeating a block of code for as long as a test stays true, including how the loop is set up beforehand and what happens when the test never turns false.

name: For Loops and Iteration
description: Walking through each item of a string, list or other sequence with a for statement instead of managing a counter by hand.

name: Counting with range()
description: Producing a run of integers from a start value, up to a stop value, in steps, to drive a counting loop, and how the stop value is treated.

name: Nested Loops
description: Placing one loop inside another so the inner one starts over on every pass of the outer one, for example to walk a grid or build a table of combinations.

name: Exiting and Skipping Loop Passes
description: Statements that end a loop early or jump straight to the next pass, and the role of an early exit in a loop that has no natural end.

name: Else Clauses on Loops
description: A clause attached to a loop that runs only when the loop finished all its passes without being cut short, handy for search-style code.

name: Defining and Calling Functions
description: Creating reusable named blocks of code with a header and an indented body, running them from elsewhere, and why splitting a program into functions keeps it easier to maintain.

name: Local and Global Variables
description: Where a name can be seen in a program: names created at the top level versus names created inside a function, and what happens when the two share a name.

name: Function Parameters and Arguments
description: How values are handed to a function, the difference between the placeholder names and the actual values, using several of them, and what happens when the value passed in is a list that the function changes.

name: Return Values
description: Sending a result back to the caller, what a function hands back when it has no result statement, and functions that can finish in several places.

name: Keyword and Default Arguments
description: Naming arguments in a call so their order does not matter, and giving parameters fallback values that apply when the caller leaves them out.

name: Redox Reactions and Electron Carriers
description: Cells pull energy out of food by moving electrons between molecules; small shuttle molecules pick up those electrons and carry them to where they are needed.

name: ATP as the Cell's Energy Currency
description: The small molecule that powers work inside cells, how breaking off a phosphate releases usable energy, and how the cell rebuilds it from its spent form.

name: Glycolysis
description: The ten-step pathway in the cytoplasm that splits one six-carbon sugar into two three-carbon molecules, first spending ATP and then earning more back along with NADH.

name: Pyruvate Oxidation
description: The link step between glycolysis and the next pathway: pyruvate enters the mitochondrion and is converted into a two-carbon unit attached to coenzyme A, giving off CO2.

name: Krebs Cycle
description: The cyclic series of reactions in the mitochondrial matrix that fully oxidizes acetyl groups, producing carbon dioxide, reduced carriers and a little ATP or GTP.

name: Electron Transport Chain
description: A series of protein complexes in the inner mitochondrial membrane that pass electrons down to oxygen while pumping protons, the last stage of aerobic breakdown.

name: ATP Synthase and the Proton Gradient
description: How a difference in hydrogen ion concentration across a membrane is used by a rotating enzyme to attach phosphate to ADP.

name: ATP Yield from Glucose
description: Adding up how many ATP one glucose molecule can ultimately produce, and why the figure is a range rather than a fixed number.

name: Fermentation and Anaerobic Respiration
description: How cells keep making energy when oxygen is absent, either by recycling NAD+ through lactate or ethanol production or by using a different final electron acceptor.

name: Fueling Respiration with Proteins and Fats
description: How starches, amino acids and triglycerides feed into the same energy-releasing pathways at different entry points.

name: Feedback Control of Cellular Respiration
description: How the cell speeds up or slows its energy-releasing pathways in response to its own energy status, mainly by adjusting a few key enzymes.

name: Pavlov's Classical Conditioning
description: Learning by association: a neutral cue comes to trigger a reflex-like reaction after being repeatedly paired with something that naturally triggers it, as first shown with salivating dogs.

name: Extinction, Generalization and Discrimination
description: What happens to a learned association over time and across similar cues: it fades when the pairing stops, can resurface after a pause, spreads to lookalike stimuli, or stays tied to the original one.

name: Watson and Little Albert
description: The founder of behaviorism and his infant experiment that produced a fear of a white rat, raising questions about ethics and about how phobias form.

name: Operant Conditioning and Skinner
description: Learning driven by consequences: behavior followed by a good outcome becomes more likely and behavior followed by a bad outcome becomes less likely, from Thorndike's cats to the Skinner box.

name: Reinforcement versus Punishment
description: Four ways of changing behavior by adding or removing something pleasant or unpleasant, and why people mix up taking away an unpleasant thing with disciplining.

name: Schedules of Reinforcement
description: The pattern of when rewards are delivered, after a set number of responses or amount of time versus unpredictably, and how each pattern shapes response rate and persistence.

name: Gambling and the Brain
description: Why slot machines and betting hook people: unpredictable payoffs, the brain's reward chemistry, and whether compulsive betting counts as an addiction.

name: Bandura and Observational Learning
description: Picking up behavior by watching a model, the stages that have to happen before a copy appears, and the doll experiment on children and aggression.

name: Stages of Memory: Sensory, Short-Term, Long-Term
description: The multi-store view of how information flows from brief registration through a limited-capacity holding area into a durable store, plus the working-memory refinement.

name: Explicit and Implicit Memory
description: Two kinds of lasting memory: facts and events you can deliberately recall versus skills and automatic associations that show up without trying to remember.

name: Encoding Information
description: How experience gets turned into a memory trace by automatic and effortful routes, and why meaning, imagery and sound influence how well it sticks.

name: Brain Structures for Memory
description: The regions that help form and store memories, among them the almond-shaped emotion center and the seahorse-shaped structure, and what rat experiments revealed about where traces live.

name: Amnesia
description: Loss of memory from injury or disease, and the difference between losing the past and being unable to form new memories.

name: Eyewitness Testimony and False Memories
description: How recollections are rebuilt rather than replayed, how leading questions and lineups can distort them, and what this means for crimes and courtrooms.

name: Why We Forget
description: Reasons memories fail, from never being encoded to fading with time, being blocked or confused with others, and a catalogue of everyday memory errors.

name: Mnemonic Devices and Chunking
description: Practical tricks that make material easier to hold, such as grouping, acronyms, rhymes, vivid imagery and the memory palace.
